text:
maria: Heads up — on today's canary I noticed several requests showing up as "unattributed" in the console sampling view. Quota anchors look wrong for SA keys.
alex: ugh. Is this the sampling layer dropping the origin header or our attribution join?
samir: I pulled a raw span — the request had X-Origin: project/none and the key id in headers, but the aggregation step matched to org-level because project was missing. Seems deterministic sampling + join order edgecase.
maria: exact. When sampling is applied before we enrich with project claim, we end up with a bad sample set and dashboards undercount project usage. That breaks canary rollouts for dedicated customers.
jeff: can you paste the query/log that reproduces the mismatch?
samir: sure — here's a simplified repro from the telemetry pipeline:```sql
-- sampling applied early
WITH sampled AS (
  SELECT * FROM requests WHERE bernoulli(0.005) -- early sample
)
SELECT sampled.key_id, enrich_project(requests.headers) as project FROM sampled JOIN requests ON sampled.id = requests.id;
```
jeff: oh wow. sampling()/bernoulli before enrichment is the culprit. We need either deterministic sampling on key_id (so enrichment order doesn't matter) or postpone sampling until after enrichment.
maria: preference is deterministic sampling on the key id so we preserve even small customers for attribution. Less ET cost and stable across retries.
alex: tradeoff — deterministic sampling increases correlation with heavy keys; could bias tests. But it fixes attribution. Maybe use two-tier: deterministic hash(key_id) for attribution sampling + uniform sample for rate metrics?
samir: implementation note: hashing on a token string in streaming code is cheap. We currently use jittered request-level random which is cheap too.
ops-bot: reminder — canary window 16:00-18:00 UTC, will auto-rollback on error rate > 1.5%. :warning:
maria: proposal: change pipeline to compute sample_bucket = hash(key_id) % 10000 and keep rows where sample_bucket < 50 (0.5%) for attribution flows. Continue the 0.5% random sample for perf metrics.
jeff: sounds reasonable. Add migration plan: backfill last 7 days for charts? Or start forward-only and annotate dashboards as "post-deterministic-sampling". Backfill would be heavy.
alex: forward-only with clear dashboard note + small UI flag in console that toggles "include pre-migration data" should be fine. Ops can hold off on SLAs for 48h.
maria: I'll open a PR with the code change + dashboard flag. Also adding a unit test to ensure project enrichment always runs before quota attribution.
samir: test suggestion: fuzz headers with missing project key and assert deterministic hash yields same sample decision across replays.
jeff: thanks. If anyone hits production noise, ping #eng-oncall and tag me.
maria: thanks team. I'll post PR link here once ready. :thumbsup:
